name: Twill Marches

stars.name: Twill A
stars.notes: Sol-like anchor of the system; steady, quiet, and generous with light, which is all the settlers ever asked.

stars.name: Twill B
stars.notes: Red companion at 55 AU; its occasional flares are the only weather the outer marches ever get.

planets.name: Burnish
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Twill A close to the fire; prospectors once hoped for rare metals and found only slag.

planets.name: Longgarth
planets.notes: Inhabited S-type world of Twill A in the mid habitable band; grain plains and orchard terraces support some ninety thousand independent farmers.

planets.name: Reedyard
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Twill A beyond Longgarth; a storm-wrapped ocean reserve protected by settler compact law from all extraction.

planets.name: Sheafholm
planets.notes: Outer S-type planet of Twill A; dry canyonlands used for seasonal grazing runs under dome-less hardy breeds.

planets.name: Dimmock
planets.notes: S-type orbit of Twill B near the red star's faint warm line; tidally locked, its dusk band holds automated volatile wells.

planets.name: Marchwind
planets.notes: Circumbinary P-type giant enclosing both stars in a wide stable orbit; balloon skimmers harvest helium for the homestead fleet.

planets.name: Highpile
planets.notes: Outermost P-type body on the marches' cold rim; its beacon marks the edge of compact patrol responsibility, such as it is.

asteroid_belts.name: The Scutching Grounds
asteroid_belts.notes: A cleared chaotic gap between the two stars' planetary families where homesteaders pan cometary fragments for water ice.

stations.name: Marchmeet
stations.notes: Bolt-together market and drydock raised by three generations of farm cooperatives; doubles as the compact's assembly hall.

faction_control.notes: Governed by the Marchmeet Compact of settler cooperatives; no charter, crown, or combine holds title, though surveyors keep re-measuring as if one might.

history: Settled by dissenting farmers who walked away from charter law rather than renew tenancy, arriving in refitted freighters that never left orbit.
A flare outburst from Twill B in the settlement's third decade burned out the outer well fields and taught the compact to insure against their own sun's companion.
The compact's petition for a formal protectorate was denied for the fourth time last year, a refusal most settlers celebrate with a festival.
description: A patient yellow star pours even light across the grain plains of Longgarth while its small red companion smolders far out like a banked stove. Seven worlds thread the system: rocky cinders near the fire, farm and reserve worlds in the comfortable middle, and wide circumbinary giants marching the cold rim. The whole layout is so textbook-stable that survey academies use it as an exam question.

Ninety thousand farmers hold the marches without a landlord, selling surplus grain through Marchmeet and arguing land policy at the same tables they eat on. Traffic is light but regular, mostly grain hulls, helium skimmers, and the occasional immigrant family with more hope than manifest. The compact protects Reedyard's storm-oceans by law, and poachers test that law every season.

Rimward cartographers keep redrawing the frontier to include the marches, and the compact keeps filing polite objections nobody reads. Rumor says a combine has begun buying old freighter debt specifically from marcher families, and no one can prove what the paper is for. Out past Highpile, beacons have started logging returns from transponders that were scrapped years ago.
